title: BIOPLASTICNET: Visual Representation Learning with Local Plasticity, Associative Memory, and Recurrent Top-Down Feedback
content: Biological visual systems acquire object representations through local synaptic plasticity, lateral competition, recurrent feedback, and memory-guided refinement—mechanisms that differ fundamentally from end-to-end gradient optimisation. Despite sustained research on biologically plausible learning, gradient-free visual systems remain substantially less accurate than backpropagation-trained networks. A natural explanation is that existing gradient-free models adopt individual biological mechanisms in isolation, whereas the biological visual system operates as a coordinated ensemble. We test this architectural composition hypothesis by introducing BIOPLASTICNET, a large-scale hierarchical vision model in which all representational parameters are updated without backpropagation. The architecture composes four local plasticity rules and four local regularising terms across seven parallel multi-frequency ventral streams on an 80×80 topographic grid, augmented by a saliency-gated dorsal pathway, a Modern Hopfield associative memory [35], and three-pathway recurrent top-down feedback. The plasticity rules include unitary-FFT holographic binding, Möbius-additive hyperbolic binding in the Poincaré ball, and Haar-wavelet binding, each also available in an Oja-normalised variant. Only a linear classification probe—approximately 0.027% of total parameters—is trained with gradient descent; all remaining weights are updated through local co-activation statistics, winner-take-all competition, attention-weighted memory updates, and local Hebbian feedback rules. To anchor this claim we ran a random-feature control: a linear probe on the identical architecture with all plasticity disabled (η0=0, fixed random weights). It reaches 51.6% on CIFAR-10—far above the 10% chance level, and roughly half of what the full system eventually achieves. Turning plasticity back on lifts this to 82.0%, a gain of approximately 30pp that is doing real, load-bearing work rather than polishing an already-sufficient front end. On CIFAR-100, Caltech-101, and Caltech-256 the full system reaches 59.7%, 70.7%, and 50.8% (n=14 seeds, BCa 95% CIs). A systematic leave-one-out and greedy-construction ablation then asks where the remaining gain comes from, and the answer is architecture, not rule choice: multi-frequency streaming, associative memory, and recurrent feedback each move the needle more than any single plasticity term, and the plasticity terms themselves turn out to be gracefully redundant with one another, in a manner reminiscent of biological degeneracy [11]. Put together, the story is a chain: a structured fixed architecture sets a strong floor, local plasticity supplies the largest single jump above it, and architectural composition—not the particular choice of binding rule—accounts for what’s left. The system is not parameter-efficient (≈3.28B representational parameters) and does not approach state-of-the-art supervised accuracy. It is offered as a calibrated systems-level reference point for the gradient-isolated learning literature and as a modular platform for neuromorphic vision research.
